name: Pan (Polish)
description: Pan is a Polish shedding game with a 24-card pack. The 9 of hearts starts the play pile. Players play cards equal to or higher than the top, or pick up. Last player holding cards gets a letter (P-A-N); first to spell the word loses.

overview.description: Pan is a Polish shedding game with a 24-card pack. The 9 of hearts starts the play pile. Players play cards equal to or higher than the top, or pick up. Last player holding cards gets a letter (P-A-N); first to spell the word loses.

history.origins: Polish card game. 'Pan' means gentleman (euphemism). Unrelated to American Panguingue.
timeline: April 2017: Rules first published in English.
Present: Played online and in Polish communities.
history.cultural: Commonly known by a vulgar name; Pan and 'Dupa Biskupa' are euphemisms.
history.evolution: Variants include max three-card pickup and optional three-equals-higher play.

setup.deck: 24-card French pack (A-K-Q-J-10-9). Rank: A (high) to 9 (low). Suits irrelevant except 9â™¥.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards as equally as possible: 2 players = 12 each, 3 = 8 each, 4 = 6 each, 5 = 4+5 each, 6 = 4 each.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards. Last player holding cards receives a letter (P, A, or N). First to spell P-A-N loses the game.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Start**: Holder of 9â™¥ plays it (and any other 9s) to start the pile. 2. **Play**: Play one card â‰¥ top, or three equal to top, or four equal higher than top. 3. **Pick up**: Take cards from pile. If >3 on 9â™¥: must take at least top 3; 9â™¥ stays. If â‰¤3 on 9â™¥: take all except 9â™¥. 4. **Turn**: When cards on pile, next player may always choose to pick up instead of playing. 5. **Out**: Players with no cards drop out. Last two: if one empties and other plays out in one turn = draw; else holder loses and gets a letter.

strategy.basic: Play high cards early to avoid picking up large piles. Save duplicates for three- or four-card plays.
strategy.intermediate: Time pickups to get useful cards. Force opponents to pick up by playing high.
strategy.advanced: Track which cards have been played; block opponents from going out.
tips: Playing four equal cards clears a lot of cards in one turn.
Pick up when the pile has cards you need.
In the endgame, holding one high card can force the opponent to pick up.

scoring.description: Elimination. Last with cards gets one letter. First to P-A-N loses the game.
